title: Label list columns and say when rows are hidden
lead: `slicer list` prints rows with no header. An unset effort is `-`, in the same line as the score. An empty default list says `no matching items` and does not mention the done and retired rows it hid.
**Not in this slice:** which statuses are hidden, the JSON array shape, sort order, or the TUI.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The columns are number, id, status, size, effort, score, quadrant, and title, and nothing in the text output names them. Reading `-` as a missing effort took a follow-up question. When every item is done or retired, the command looks like a failed filter. `slicer status` has the census, but `list` is the command people run.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`cmd_list` and `_item_rows`)
- the list tests
- `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` if the text shape is part of the documented contract

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A non-empty text list starts with one header line that names effort and score. An item with no effort still shows `-` under effort.
2. When the default filter hides done or retired rows, the text says how many were hidden and names `--all`. JSON remains the array of visible items, with no extra keys.
3. `--all`, a `--status` filter, and an empty project do not claim that rows were hidden when none were.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add a single header row to the text list. When the default status filter omits at least one item, append one line with the hidden count and `--all`. Keep JSON as the list of item records. Do not add the header to `--json` output. Match the header to the row fields, including the effort column only if the row still prints effort.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The three cases above pass. `slicer list --json` of a project that hides done items is still a JSON array. The suite and `slicer check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
